subject: Protective off-ramp language and staggered downgrade schedule — exec sign-off needed
messages:
From: Grace Liu <grace.liu@medsavvy.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedSavvy Legal <legal@medsavvy.com>
Date: 2027-03-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal questions — ramp and off-ramp

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for walking us through the proposal yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our side: we need clearer language around early termination and the ramp commitment. The execs are uncomfortable with a hard 12-month committed run rate without a safe, staged off-ramp if the POC doesn’t deliver against latency/cost targets.

High-level asks from MedSavvy:
- A 3-stage ramp schedule for the first 6 months (Pilot, Growth, Committed) with explicit thresholds.
- A 60-day opt-out clause after month 6 with prorated credits rather than full termination fees.
- Downsell protections so we can reduce committed capacity by up to 40% at each 3-month checkpoint without penalty (provided notice).

I attached a redlined SOW that shows what we had in mind. Can Redwood provide suggested contract language and confirm whether the protective off-ramp would be limited to pilots or could be applied to initial commercial terms?

Best,
Grace
Senior Product Lead, MedSavvy Health

Attachments: MedSavvy_SOW_Draft_20270328.pdf (PDF, 128KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposal questions — ramp and off-ramp (need exec guidance)

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Grace's note and the attached redline. MedSavvy is asking for a fairly generous staged off-ramp and explicit downsell protections. Quick summary of proposed concessions: 

- Ramp cadence: Pilot (0-2 months), Growth (3-6 months), Committed (>6 months) with capacity/price tiers.
- 60-day opt-out after month 6 with prorated credits rather than termination fees.
- Ability to downsize committed capacity by up to 40% at each quarter checkpoint with 30-day notice.
- Non-standard discounting tied to commit levels (they're requesting a blended effective price lower than our standard table).

I'm OK offering a protective off-ramp for pilot customers, but we need executive sign-off for credits & precedence on downsell language. I proposed a middle ground in the attached "Redwood-Protective-Offramp-Draft-v3.docx": cap total credit liability at 20% of first-year commit, require ROI metrics for the pilot (latency <120ms p95, cost per token delta <10% vs baseline), and make the downsell protection available only during the first 12 months.

Can you weigh in on acceptable caps/edits and whether we should route this via legal + finance before returning to MedSavvy?

Thanks — Tessa
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-Protective-Offramp-Draft-v3.docx (DOCX, 45KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-28T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposal questions — ramp and off-ramp (need exec guidance)

Tessa — thanks for flagging. My concerns: we should avoid an open-ended template that other reps reuse to erode ARR. Specific suggestions:

- Keep the 60-day opt-out but replace "prorated credits" with a capped credit bucket equal to 15% of committed spend for year 1 (this is easier for finance).
- Limit the downsell protection to a one-time 30-40% downsizing within the first 9 months, not at each checkpoint; repeat downsells set precedent.
- Require customer-signed performance playbook with monthly check-ins; if metrics aren't met, we trigger the off-ramp automatically (protects both sides).

If we accept their discount ask, we should require a stepped discount waterfall (Pilot discount, then step-down if they commit to year 2). Also recommend legal carve the clause to apply to "Pilot and initial commercial term only".

If you're comfortable with those edits, I'll loop in Legal (Olga) and Finance (Logan) for final numbers. We should also capture the deal in Deal Desk (DEAL-1394) so it appears in the precedent tracker.

-Marissa
Director, Deal Desk

Thanks for the context and the draft language. I agree with Marissa's approach with one modification to reduce friction for closing: allow a one-time downsizing at the 6- to 9-month checkpoint up to 30% (not repeatable), capped credit liability at 18% of year-1 committed spend, and require the signed performance playbook as a gating condition. Legal and Finance are cc'd to confirm the numbers and finalize language.

Approved conditionally:
- Cap credits at 18% of year-1 commit (Logan to confirm accounting treatment).
- Downsizing allowed once within months 6–9 up to 30% with 30-day notice; no additional downsizes without renewal.
- 60-day opt-out remains but triggers the capped credit bucket only if the signed performance playbook shows the agreed metrics weren't met.
- Clause limited to Pilot + Initial Commercial Term (first 12 months).

Next steps: Tessa, send updated SOW with these edits; Olga/Legal to finalize clause language and log precedent in Deal Desk. Once legal and finance confirm, we can present a final redline to MedSavvy.

-Karthik
VP, Sales Operations
